cases.name: batch-two-long
texts: Distributed inference partitions a trained neural network between workers. The first worker applies the embedding layer and the first three transformer layers. It serializes hidden activations using a bounded binary format. The second worker continues the remaining three layers and pools a sentence vector. The coordinator compares the result against the original model in one process. Ledger accounting is timed separately from numerical computation, transport and serialization. No mining network or public chain is involved. A cryptographic hash records a statement but cannot establish that the statement is correct. Verification needs explicit assumptions and a method to resolve disagreement.

This benchmark uses CPU inference on one machine with persistent child processes. Model download and initialization are excluded from warm measurements and reported separately. A fixed workload and model revision make comparisons reproducible. Warm-up precedes alternating local and split runs. The report retains individual observations instead of showing only a favorable average. Serialization, process communication, forward computation and local ledger calls each consume time. An embedding model can support semantic retrieval without generating text. More workers do not automatically improve latency. This study measures overhead and equivalence, without claiming a quality benchmark or distributed speedup.
